This is a subverse dedicated to helping people get a handle on their budget and make improvements. We live in a society that has made talking about money taboo. It is often detrimental to our financial well being and hinders us from learning about how to manage our money wisely. We aim to provide a space where people can talk openly about their budget and money and receive constructive criticism and feedback.

Feel free to create a throw-away account.

There are several different categories that can be posted here, depending on what you're looking for:

[Case Study] - Use this when asking for advice on an existing fully defined budget. List income, pre-tax deductions, all expenses, outstanding loans and their interest rate and the payment on those loans, and what your liability and assets are worth. Include details of where you are in life, your goals, what questions you have and what improvements you already know you need to make.

[Creation]- Not sure where to start? Ask some questions on how to start creating a budget and we will point you in the right direction! Provide as many details as possible and we will help point the way.

[Critique] - If you already have a general budget, but would like some critique on where you may have over-allocated, under-allocated or if the budget is generally realistic, ask for a Critique. This will help you more accurately define your budget and see where you might be missing things.

[Budget Question]- General catch all for any other questions relating to budgeting.

---Recommended Budget Software---

At the end of the day, use what works for you. If you don't use the software or the technique, then it is worthless to you.

Budget Advice recommends using an application called You Need a Budget (YNAB) to help create your budget and track your spending. It's a very powerful program and comes with a lot of training videos and great advice. Students can get this application for free.

After your budget is created, Mint.com provides a very robust reporting system so you can track your Net Worth, investments and historical trends. Mint, in my opinion, is NOT a budgeting tool. It is a historical trend analytics tool to see how you've changed and grown.

Finally, spreadsheets like Google Spreadsheet or Microsoft Excel are great tools to get started on figuring out your budget and where your money is going. I personally enjoy YNAB more.

---Principals---

There are some core principals that Budget Advice adheres to:

  • All debt is an emergency that should be your first priority.
  • Live well below your means.
  • Everyone makes mistakes and life throws curve balls. Be flexible.
  • Separate out needs from wants - most things are wants.
  • We are a positive, helpful community. Negativity and hate will not be tolerated here.
